about: Anchored HUD clusters for ui_layout.py (w733). Each member is the union of everything drawn under that object; its edges are measured against the anchor's, and a change over the tolerance between before and after fails. Names are object names in main.unity (HudCornerSpacing.cs names the bottom-right ones). OptionToggles is the column of slide-out toggles; its parent QuckControls also holds the slide-outs themselves, which move when opened, so it is not a member. The edges key limits a cluster to the edges that should hold (a panel whose height follows its content keeps only its left and top). Add a cluster when you change one. openedPanels classifies the elements a player opens on purpose and can close (w742): they may cover the HUD, and ui_layout.py checks them instead of counting their overlaps.

openedPanels.why: A panel or slide-out the player opens on purpose and can close may draw over HUD elements (the hotbar, the Objectives card, the minimap buttons). ui_layout.py does not count its overlaps with the HUD; it checks that the panel draws on top, takes the clicks over everything it covers, stays inside the screen, and that closing it leaves the covered HUD where it was. Overlaps between always-on HUD blocks, anchored-cluster drift and colour mismatches still fail.
who: Ben, w732, 2026-10-09: "Put the slide out back just make it appear over the hot bar. The user can then close it to show the hotbar again"
Ben, w742, 2026-10-09, on the Blueprints window covering the Objectives card: "the blueprint panel showing over objectives is fine since its a temporarily opened panel"
openedPanels.howToAdd: Add a path (components joined with /, fnmatch globs, matched against a run of components anywhere in the element's path, '(Clone)' ignored) only for something the player opens on purpose and can close again. Never for something always showing, and never to make a check pass: a HUD piece in the way of another HUD piece is a defect.
